name: Paints & Coatings
tagline: Interior, wood and metal systems — specified by film, not by colour
description: Colour is the easy part. What decides whether a paint job still looks right in three years is the system: the primer, the number of coats, the sheen level and whether the surface underneath was ever properly prepared. Wood and metal coatings are listed here too, because those are the finishes that fail first.

materials.name: Interior emulsion
materials.description: The everyday interior finish: two coats over primer on a putty-finished wall. Mid-range emulsions now wash well enough for most family homes without moving to a luxury grade.

materials.name: Luxury emulsion
materials.blurb: Richer film, better wash resistance, deeper colours
materials.description: Higher binder and pigment loading gives a smoother film that scrubs without polishing up. Worth the upgrade in corridors, kids' rooms and anywhere hands touch the wall daily.

materials.name: Matt finish paint
materials.blurb: Flat sheen that hides an imperfect wall
materials.description: The lowest sheen level, which scatters light and forgives undulations in plaster. Harder to clean than a sheen finish, so keep it above the touch line.

materials.name: Satin / silk finish paint
materials.blurb: Low-sheen, wipeable finish for high-touch walls
materials.description: A gentle sheen that resists marks and cleans easily — the sensible choice for kitchens, dining rooms and stairwells. It will, however, show every bump in the plaster.

materials.name: Texture paint
materials.blurb: Heavy-bodied decorative coating applied with tools
materials.description: Trowel, roller or spatula applied compounds that build a physical texture — travertine, stucco, dragged and combed effects. A skilled applicator matters more than the brand.

materials.name: Designer finish
materials.blurb: Metallic, pearl and special-effect decorative coatings
materials.description: Brand-specific effect ranges — metallic sheens, pearl washes, concrete looks. Sample them on site under the actual lighting; they behave nothing like the swatch card in a showroom.

materials.name: PU coating (wood)
materials.blurb: Polyurethane finish — the premium wood coating
materials.description: A hard, chemical-resistant film that keeps timber looking wet-rich for years. Available matte through gloss, and the standard specification for veneered joinery in premium homes.

materials.name: Melamine polish
materials.blurb: Traditional wood finish — cheaper and faster than PU
materials.description: The long-standing Indian carpenter's finish: quick to apply, easy to touch up, less durable and more brittle than PU. Fine for low-contact joinery and tight budgets.

materials.name: Duco paint
materials.blurb: Sprayed opaque finish for a seamless painted shutter
materials.description: Multiple sprayed coats sanded between passes give a factory-smooth painted surface on MDF. Slow, dusty and expensive on site — best done in a workshop.

materials.name: NC lacquer
materials.blurb: Fast-drying nitrocellulose finish for quick turnarounds
materials.description: Dries in minutes, which makes it the go-to for site work and repairs. Softer and less chemical-resistant than PU, and it yellows with age.

materials.name: Wood stain
materials.blurb: Penetrating colour that keeps the grain visible
materials.description: Changes the tone of timber without hiding it — the way a pale ash becomes smoked grey or a mango wood reads as walnut. Always trial on an offcut of the actual batch.

materials.name: Enamel paint (metal)
materials.blurb: Oil-based gloss for grilles, gates and railings
materials.description: The traditional metal finish: tough, glossy and easy to reapply, over a red-oxide or zinc primer. Yellows over time in interior positions, so keep it outside where it belongs.

materials.name: PU coating (metal)
materials.blurb: Two-pack polyurethane for durable, colour-fast metalwork
materials.description: Holds colour and gloss far longer than enamel under Indian sun, which is why it is specified on architectural metalwork and MS frames that must not be repainted every year.

materials.name: Powder coating
materials.blurb: Oven-baked electrostatic finish — the toughest metal coat
materials.description: Powder applied electrostatically and cured in an oven, giving a hard, even film with no runs. Must be done off site, so all fabrication and drilling has to be finished first.

materials.name: Wall putty
materials.blurb: The base coat that decides how good the paint looks
materials.description: Two coats of white cement or acrylic putty, sanded flat, is what separates a smooth wall from a patchy one. Skipping it to save money is the most common reason a paint job disappoints.
